headline: Pool destocking crushes profit, tariff refunds cushion blow
summary_short: Pentair reported Q2 FY2026 sales of $932.6M, down 17.0% y/y and 10.0% q/q as Pool-channel inventory destocking cut deeply into results, with diluted EPS falling 11.1% y/y to $0.80 despite a roughly $35M IEEPA tariff-refund benefit.
summary_long: Pentair's preliminary Q2 results fell well short of its own prior guidance, driven almost entirely by Pool-segment channel destocking: management estimates the inventory realignment cut Q2 Pool sales by about $170M and Pool segment income by about $105M, while Flow and Water Solutions performed roughly in line with plan. A roughly $35M IEEPA tariff refund partly offset the hit. Revenue fell to $932.6M (-17.0% y/y), operating income to $166.5M (-23.5% y/y), and diluted EPS to $0.80 (-11.1% y/y). The company cut full-year 2026 guidance (adjusted EPS to $4.60-$4.80 from $5.30-$5.40) and repurchased $150M of shares in the quarter. CFO Nicholas Brazis departed July 10; Bob Fishman returned as interim CFO.

drivers.explanation: Pentair attributes the quarter's shortfall almost entirely to a more pronounced Pool channel inventory realignment than previously estimated, plus worsening business conditions (higher interest rates, inflation); Flow and Water Solutions performed roughly in line with prior guidance.
The company estimates Pool-channel inventory destocking cut Pool segment sales by about $170M in the quarter, versus a previous guide of sales up approximately 1%.
Pool destocking cut Pool segment income by about $105M; partly offset by roughly $35M of IEEPA tariff refunds recognized in the quarter.
EPS of approximately $0.80 versus previous guidance of $1.39-$1.42 reflects the same Pool destocking impact partly offset by the IEEPA refund, per the company's own guidance revision.
